clue.text: Rough spherical object found by recreation ground

parts.note: a ball is a round object
a park is a public recreation ground

explanation.surface: Someone comes across a battered ball lying next to the local playing field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rough' looks like a description of the ball but it is the definition, as in a ballpark figure.
explanation.definitionFit: A ballpark figure is an approximate estimate, so the adjective means approximate or rough.

clue.text: Row right up close to craft on the rocks

parts.note: a bank is a row, as of oars or keys

indicators.note: close to points to the last letter of the word craft

explanation.surface: Oarsmen pull a boat up near a vessel stuck on rocks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' is a noun, a line, not rowing; 'on the rocks' means financially ruined, not shipwrecked.
explanation.definitionFit: A business on the rocks is failing, insolvent and unable to pay its debts.

clue.text: Gallons stored in Asian country port

indicators.note: stored in says the gallons go inside the country

parts.note: Laos is a country in South-East Asia

explanation.surface: Fuel is kept in a harbour of an Asian state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Asian country port' reads as one place, but the port is in Nigeria.
explanation.definitionFit: Lagos is Nigeria's largest city and a major seaport.

clue.text: Foolish to stay up in German city

indicators.note: up in a down clue says the letters are read from the bottom

parts.note: mad means foolish
to stop is to stay somewhere

explanation.surface: It is silly to remain awake in some German town.
explanation.definitionFit: Potsdam is a city near Berlin, site of the 1945 conference.

clue.text: Function of pitch, reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly says the word is said aloud, sounding like another

parts.note: a ship's pitch and roll are both motions at sea

explanation.surface: The purpose of a sports field, so it is said.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pitch' suggests a sports field, but here it is a ship's motion, paired with roll.
explanation.definitionFit: A role is the job or purpose something serves.

clue.text: Not charged, deserter held by American soldiers

indicators.note: held by says the deserter sits inside the soldiers

parts.note: GIs are US soldiers
a rat is someone who deserts a cause

explanation.surface: A deserter arrested by US troops is released without charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not charged' suggests a legal release; here it means free of payment.
explanation.definitionFit: Something given free costs nothing, so no charge is made for it.

clue.text: Remainder to lodge round university

indicators.note: round says the lodging verb wraps about the university

parts.note: to lodge is to reside

explanation.surface: A student left over goes into lodgings near campus.
explanation.definitionFit: A residue is what is left over, a remnant.

clue.text: Sailor, man wearing waterproof stuff

parts.note: tar is an old word for a sailor
Paul is a man's name
in means wearing, as in a coat

explanation.surface: A seaman dressed in oilskins.
explanation.definitionFit: A tarpaulin is heavy proofed canvas used as a cover against rain.

clue.text: Few and far between, boxes on foremost of estates

parts.note: spars is to box, to fight with fists

indicators.note: foremost of points to the opening letter of the word estates

explanation.surface: Thin pickings: packing crates sit on the best estates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boxes' is a verb, fights, not containers.
explanation.definitionFit: Something thinly scattered is scarce, rarely found.

clue.text: Bad thing, weapon used in disco

indicators.note: bad suggests the letters of the next word are spoilt and rearranged

parts.note: a club is a blunt weapon

explanation.surface: A nasty object, a cudgel, is wielded at a dance venue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bad' rearranges THING to NIGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: A disco is a venue for dancing at night, a kind of nightspot.

clue.text: Everyone, taken in by most of band, in uproar

indicators.note: taken in by says everyone sits inside the next word

parts.note: taken as written
all means everyone

indicators.note: most of says the last letter of the band is dropped

parts.note: a hoop is a circular band

explanation.surface: The whole crowd, drawn in by most of a group, is in tumult.
explanation.walkthrough: 'band' suggests musicians but is a hoop; 'by' gives its own letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Ballyhoo is noisy fuss and commotion, a hubbub.

clue.text: Country in revolutionary fairy story

indicators.note: revolutionary says the hidden letters are read backwards
in says the letters sit inside the words fairy story

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A rebel-themed fairy tale set in some nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' marks the hidden letters AIRYS, which 'revolutionary' turns round; the draft omitted that indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: Syria is a nation of the Middle East.

clue.text: Live on edge

parts.note: re means on or about
a side is an edge

explanation.surface: Someone lives a precarious life on the brink.
explanation.definitionFit: To live somewhere is to dwell there, a synonym.

clue.text: Good boys protecting kid in best clothes

indicators.note: protecting says the boys surround the kid

parts.note: lads are boys
to rag is to tease or kid

explanation.surface: Well-behaved boys shield a child dressed in Sunday best.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kid' is a verb here, tease, not a child.
explanation.definitionFit: Glad rags is an informal idiom for one's smartest outfit.

clue.text: Fellow members run into trouble with Society

indicators.note: into says the run goes inside the trouble

parts.note: bother means trouble
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Club members find themselves in difficulty with a society.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of a fraternity or union are called brethren, comrades of one body.

clue.text: Take the part of one of Silver's crew and he will be very angry

parts.note: to play a role is to take a part
George Merry is one of Long John Silver's pirates in Treasure Island
he'll is the contraction of he will

explanation.surface: An actor cast as a Treasure Island pirate will be furious about it.
explanation.walkthrough: Long John Silver is the pirate cook in Stevenson's Treasure Island; Merry is among his mutineers.
explanation.definitionFit: To raise a furious row is an idiom for venting great anger.

clue.text: Evergreen opera song about a posh limo?

indicators.note: about says the song goes round the other pieces

parts.note: an aria is a solo song in an opera
U means upper-class, posh
a limo is a kind of car

explanation.surface: A popular operatic number about an upmarket stretch limousine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Evergreen' hints at a lasting song, but is the tree; the '?' flags limo as an example of a car.
explanation.definitionFit: Araucaria is a genus of evergreen conifers, including the monkey puzzle tree.

clue.text: Famous pianist, murderess's first husband in Sayers novel

indicators.note: first points to the opening letter of the word murderess's
novel, meaning new, says the pool of letters is reshaped

explanation.surface: A detective-story plot: the killer's first spouse appears in a Dorothy L. Sayers book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sayers novel' looks like a book title; 'novel' rearranges SAYERS together with M and H.
explanation.definitionFit: Dame Myra Hess was a celebrated English concert pianist of the twentieth century.

clue.text: Fifties Kitchen sink drama — something Winnie was fond of?

definitions.meaning: Shelagh Delaney's 1958 gritty realist play set in Salford
a sample of the sweet stuff Winnie-the-Pooh loved

explanation.walkthrough: Kitchen sink drama is the British label for gritty working-class realism of the late 1950s; Winnie is Winnie-the-Pooh, the honey-loving bear.
explanation.definitionFit: The play's title, read literally, is a small sample of the bear's favourite food.

clue.text: Shorten a piece of snooker equipment

parts.note: a bridge is the rest used to support a snooker cue

explanation.surface: Cut down a cue rest.
explanation.walkthrough: In snooker, a bridge is a cue rest for long shots.
explanation.definitionFit: To abridge a text is to cut it down, a synonym of curtail.

clue.text: Short durable cape — that's the gear

indicators.note: short says the last letter of the durable word is cut

parts.note: hard means tough or durable
ness is a word for a headland or cape

explanation.surface: A short, sturdy cloak counts as the right kit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cape' is a headland, not a cloak; 'Short' cuts HARD to HAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A harness is the straps and fittings, tackle for a horse or climber.

clue.text: Bitterly cold in lorry crossing Canada's capital

indicators.note: crossing says the lorry spans the capital letter

parts.note: an artic is an articulated lorry, a British truck

indicators.note: capital points to the opening letter of the word Canada's

explanation.surface: Freezing conditions for a truck driving through Ottawa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' suggests Ottawa but means the first letter, C.
explanation.definitionFit: Arctic describes polar, freezing conditions.

clue.text: Judge's pipe

definitions.meaning: in England a part-time criminal court judge holds this title
a simple woodwind instrument played by schoolchildren

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a part-time judge and an end-blown wooden flute.

clue.text: In section of sea, notice a large fleet

parts.note: an arm of the sea is an inlet
an ad is an advertisement or notice

explanation.surface: Out on an inlet, someone spots a vast flotilla.
explanation.walkthrough: 'notice' is the noun, an advertisement, not the verb to spot.
explanation.definitionFit: An armada is a great assembly of warships, like the Spanish one of 1588.

clue.text: Similar article to enjoy

parts.note: a is the indefinite article
to like something is to enjoy it

explanation.surface: A comparable item to savour.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that are similar are much the same as each other.

clue.text: Eccentric queen, for example

definitions.meaning: an odd or amusing person is called this
the queen is one of a pack of playing pieces

explanation.surface: An odd monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a quirky character and also a playing piece such as a queen.

clue.text: Played out, even across river

indicators.note: across says the even piece stretches over the river

parts.note: tied means level or even in score

explanation.surface: A drawn match continues over the river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Played out' reads like a finished game, but means exhausted.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone played out is exhausted, worn and weary.

clue.text: Announce team in the USA

parts.note: to state is to announce
a side is a team

explanation.surface: A sports squad is named for a match in America.
explanation.definitionFit: Stateside is an informal adverb meaning in or toward America.

clue.text: County town originally producing a red wine

parts.note: Clare is a county in western Ireland

indicators.note: originally points to the opening letter of the word town

explanation.surface: A provincial centre is the birthplace of some red wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'County town' looks like one phrase but splits: Clare is the Irish county.
explanation.definitionFit: Claret is the British name for red Bordeaux.

clue.text: You almost sussed out Greek hero

indicators.note: out signals the letters are rearranged, put out of order
almost says the last letter of the word you is dropped

explanation.surface: Someone nearly figured out who the Greek hero was.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims YOU to YO, and 'out' rearranges YO with SUSSED.
explanation.definitionFit: Homer's Odyssey tells of this Greek warrior's long voyage home from Troy.
